data.main_content_0_1:
| The Linux kernel manages the processor, memory, interrupts, hardware drivers, networking and filesystems. Applications use kernel services and do not control most hardware directly. In a PHYTEC BSP the kernel is delivered together with a device tree that describes the board, a bootloader that loads both, and a root filesystem that holds the programs.
| PHYTEC maintains its own kernel repositories. They contain a Linux kernel, the silicon vendor patches (NXP or Texas Instruments) and the PHYTEC changes for its SoMs and carrier boards. The BSP release fixes one exact revision of this source. Using another revision is the most common reason for mismatched modules and missing device-tree files.
data.important_0_1_0:
| **Kernel source is not the whole system**
| A bootloader starts the system, the device tree describes the hardware, and the root filesystem holds libraries, services and applications. A kernel change helps only when those parts match it. See BSP-01 for the full picture.
data.main_content_0_2: Every kernel change follows the same path. The path splits at the end: a standalone build is fast for testing, and a Yocto-integrated build makes the change repeatable.
data.main_content_0_3: PHYTEC publishes more than one kernel repository. The right one depends on the SoC family and on the BSP line. Copying a command from a different product is the quickest way to clone the wrong source.
data.table_caption_0_3_0: Table 1. PHYTEC kernel repositories and the BSP releases that document them
data.table_0_3_0_1_1: TI-based BSPs: phyCORE-AM62x, AM62Ax, AM64x, AM67x and AM57x. Example: AM62x PD26.1.0 uses tag v6.18.38-12.01.00.05-phy6.
data.table_0_3_0_1_2: PHYTEC standalone kernel guides for AM62x, AM67x and AM57x [1] [2]
data.table_0_3_0_2_1: NXP-based i.MX 8M Plus BSP-Yocto-NXP-i.MX8MP-PD26.1.0. Example tag: v6.12.49-2.2.0-phy11.
data.table_0_3_0_2_2: PHYTEC PD26.1.0 i.MX 8M Plus guide, as cited in the earlier BSP-02 draft. Confirm the repository name in your BSP manual.
data.table_0_3_0_3_1: Mainline-based BSP lines. Example: i.MX 8M Plus PD24.1.1 uses tag v6.6.21-phy1.
data.table_0_3_0_3_2: PHYTEC i.MX 8M Plus mainline BSP documentation [3]
data.table_0_3_0_4_1: Older NXP-based lines. Example: i.MX7 PD23.1.1 uses tag v5.15.71_2.2.2-phy3.
data.warning_0_3_1:
| **Repository names change between releases**
| Older PHYTEC documents use other locations, for example stash.phytec.com for i.MX8X PD21.1.0. For i.MX 6UL and AM335x, read the repository and tag from the release notes of your own BSP. The kernel trees of both boards contain PHYTEC defconfigs, which is a useful check after cloning (see the section on PHYTEC files inside the kernel tree).
data.main_content_0_4: A PHYTEC tag names an exact revision. Read it from left to right: the Linux version, the vendor release it is based on, and the PHYTEC revision.
data.table_caption_0_4_0: Table 2. How to read PHYTEC kernel tags
data.table_0_4_0_1_2: Linux 6.18.38, TI Processor SDK release 12.01.00.05, PHYTEC revision 6. Used by AM62x PD26.1.0.
data.table_0_4_0_2_2: Linux 6.12.35, TI SDK release 11.01.05, PHYTEC revision 6. Used by AM62x and AM67x PD25.1.x.
data.table_0_4_0_4_2: Linux 6.6.21 stable plus PHYTEC revision 1. No vendor release number.
data.table_0_4_0_5_2: Linux 5.15.71, NXP release 2.2.2, PHYTEC revision 3. Used by an older i.MX7 BSP.
data.tip_0_4_1:
| **Check what you actually have**
| After cloning or in an existing tree, git describe --tags --always shows the nearest tag, and make kernelrelease shows the version the build will report. If the two disagree with the release notes, stop and find out why before you change anything.
data.main_heading_0_5: Finding the Kernel for Your BSP Release
data.main_content_0_5: Never use the newest tag in a repository by default. Use the tag of your BSP release.
data.list_items_0_5_0:
Open the release notes of your BSP. They list the kernel tag, the bootloader tag and the Yocto release.
Open the standalone kernel section of the BSP manual. For TI-based BSPs it is called Standalone Kernel Development under Building the BSP. It gives the clone command and tag for that release. [1]
Cross-check the Yocto recipe. If you have the BSP source, search the kernel recipe in the PHYTEC layer for the source URL, branch and revision (commands below).
Record the result. Keep repository, tag, defconfig and device-tree name together with the BSP release name.
data.content_0_5_0:
1. Open the release notes of your BSP. They list the kernel tag, the bootloader tag and the Yocto release.
2. Open the standalone kernel section of the BSP manual. For TI-based BSPs it is called Standalone Kernel Development under Building the BSP. It gives the clone command and tag for that release. [1]
3. Cross-check the Yocto recipe. If you have the BSP source, search the kernel recipe in the PHYTEC layer for the source URL, branch and revision (commands below).
4. Record the result. Keep repository, tag, defconfig and device-tree name together with the BSP release name.
data.main_content_0_6: Kernel builds for the target use a cross-compiler. PHYTEC delivers one in the pre-built SDK for each BSP release. Install the SDK first, then source its environment script in every new terminal.
data.table_0_6_0_3_0: i.MX 8M Plus PD26.1.0 (from the earlier draft; confirm in the manual)
data.content_0_6_1: Host packages listed by PHYTEC for Ubuntu standalone builds:
data.code_content_0_6_2:
$ sudo apt update
$ sudo apt install git build-essential bison flex libssl-dev
# only if the device-tree build reports: fatal error: yaml.h
$ sudo apt install libyaml-dev
data.content_0_6_3: After sourcing the script, check that the cross-compiler is active:
data.note_0_6_5:
| **Container builds**
| PHYTEC BSP guides often run the build inside a container. Commands that need root access to a mounted SD card, such as modules_install to /media/..., must run on the host outside the container.
data.main_heading_0_7: Cloning the Kernel and Creating a Working Branch
data.main_content_0_7: Clone the repository for your BSP line, check out the release tag, and create your own branch before editing. A tag is a fixed revision, so Git reports a detached HEAD after checking it out. Work on a branch so that commits are not lost.
data.code_content_0_7_1:
$ cd ~/BSP-Yocto-Ampliphy-AM62x-PD26.1.0
$ git clone -b v6.18.38-12.01.00.05-phy6 https://github.com/phytec/linux-phytec-ti
$ cd linux-phytec-ti
$ git checkout -b v6.18.38-12.01.00.05-phy6
data.code_content_0_7_3:
$ git clone https://github.com/phytec/linux-phytec-imx.git
$ cd linux-phytec-imx
$ git fetch --all --tags
$ git checkout tags/v6.12.49-2.2.0-phy11
$ git switch --create work/pollux-kernel-change
$ git describe --tags --always
data.warning_0_7_4:
| **Do not copy these commands to another board**
| The repository, tag, SDK path, defconfig and device-tree name are specific to these releases. For another SoC or BSP release, take them from that release notes and manual.
data.main_content_0_8: The kernel contains many directories, and most are not board specific. For PHYTEC work you mainly use the architecture directory for configuration and device trees, the drivers directory, and the device-tree binding documents.
data.table_caption_0_8_0: Table 4. Important top-level directories in a kernel tree
data.table_0_8_0_1_1: Architecture code. arch/arm/ and arch/arm64/ hold defconfigs in configs/ and device trees in boot/dts/.
data.table_0_8_0_2_1: Hardware drivers grouped by area: I²C, SPI, GPIO, network, USB, storage and more.
data.table_0_8_0_3_1: Kernel documentation, including device-tree bindings in Documentation/devicetree/bindings/.
data.table_0_8_0_4_1: Header files used by kernel code.
data.table_0_8_0_5_1: Core kernel, memory management, filesystems, networking and audio.
data.table_0_8_0_6_1: Build and configuration helper scripts, including device-tree compiler tools.
data.table_0_8_0_7_1: Top-level build rules and the root of kernel configuration options.
data.sub_head_0_8_1: PHYTEC Files Inside the Kernel Tree
data.image_desc_0_8_2: Figure 2. Kernel tree and build outputs
data.content_0_8_3:
|

The next table comes from kernel tree listings of five PHYTEC boards supplied with this guide. The listings include build outputs such as vmlinux, so they were taken after a build.
data.tip_0_8_4:
| **Layouts differ between kernel versions**
| Linux 6.5 moved ARM device trees into vendor folders such as arch/arm/boot/dts/nxp/imx/ and arch/arm/boot/dts/ti/omap/. The AM62x listing still uses the older flat arch/arm/boot/dts/ layout for ARM files, which points to an older kernel base than the others. Always search with find or grep instead of assuming a path, and confirm the version with git describe.
data.table_caption_0_8_5: Table 5. PHYTEC kernel files seen in five sample trees
data.table_0_8_5_1_3: arch/arm64/boot/Image and Image.gz; .dtb in the DTS folder
data.table_0_8_5_2_1: arch/arm/configs/imx_v6_v7_defconfig plus imx6_phytec_distro.config, imx6_phytec_machine.config and imx6_phytec_platform.config
data.table_0_8_5_4_2: k3-am62-phycore-som.dtsi; k3-am625-phyboard-lyra-rdk.dts in arch/arm64/boot/dts/ti/; overlays use .dtso files
data.table_0_8_5_4_3: arch/arm64/boot/Image; .dtb and .dtbo in the DTS folder
data.table_0_8_5_5_2: k3-am64-phycore-som.dtsi; k3-am642-phyboard-electra-rdk.dts in arch/arm64/boot/dts/ti/; overlays use .dtso files
data.table_0_8_5_5_3: Tree not yet built in the listing
data.warning_0_8_6:
| **Start from a clean tree**
| Two of the supplied listings contain files that do not belong to a clean PHYTEC checkout. The i.MX 8M Plus tree has two patch files in its root directory, and the AM335x tree holds ARM device trees in both the old flat path and the new vendor folders. Run git status and git stash list, remove or commit stray files, and rebuild from a known tag before you trust the result.
data.main_content_0_9: The kernel configuration decides which features are built in and which drivers are built as modules. A defconfig is a saved starting configuration for a platform. A config fragment (a file ending in .config) adds or changes selected options. The file .config is the result that the build actually uses. Kconfig files define the available options and their dependencies.
data.table_caption_0_9_0: Table 6. Configuration targets for the sample platforms
data.table_0_9_0_2_2: Earlier BSP-02 draft citing the PD26.1.0 guide; files confirmed in the sample tree.
data.table_0_9_0_3_2: Fragments confirmed in the sample tree; PHYTEC Wiki lists this combination for BSPs from PD20. Confirm in your BSP manual.
data.table_0_9_0_4_2: Defconfig confirmed in the sample tree.
data.content_0_9_1: A typical sequence for a TI AM6x board:
data.code_content_0_9_2:
$ make phytec_ti_defconfig       # start from the PHYTEC configuration
$ make menuconfig               # enable or disable drivers and features
$ make savedefconfig            # write a minimal defconfig file
data.list_items_0_9_3:
Use the documented PHYTEC target as the starting point. A generic defconfig may leave out board features.
After a change, check .config and the build output. An option can be dropped because of a missing dependency.
savedefconfig writes a file named defconfig in the build directory. Compare it with the original and keep only the lines that differ as a fragment or patch.
A local .config is not part of a Yocto build. See the section on tracking changes.
data.content_0_9_3:
- Use the documented PHYTEC target as the starting point. A generic defconfig may leave out board features.
- After a change, check .config and the build output. An option can be dropped because of a missing dependency.
- savedefconfig writes a file named defconfig in the build directory. Compare it with the original and keep only the lines that differ as a fragment or patch.
- A local .config is not part of a Yocto build. See the section on tracking changes.
data.main_content_0_10: With the SDK environment active and the configuration selected, one command builds the kernel image, the device trees and the modules
data.code_content_0_10_0:
$ make -j"$(nproc)"                         # Image, DTBs and modules
$ make ti/k3-am625-phyboard-lyra-rdk.dtb    # one DTB only (TI example)
$ make freescale/imx8mp-phyboard-pollux-rdk.dtb  # one DTB only (i.MX 8M Plus)
data.content_0_10_1: A single device-tree target is named relative to the architecture dts folder. Use the name of your own board file.
data.note_0_10_3:
| **FIT images on newer NXP releases**
| The newer i.MX 8M releases boot a FIT image that packs the kernel, device trees and overlays together. A plain Image copied to the boot partition is then not enough. Follow the packaging and deployment steps of your BSP manual.
data.content_0_10_4: Modules are installed into a staging root filesystem or onto the target SD card. The modules must belong to the exact kernel you will boot.
data.danger_0_10_6:
| **Keep a way back before you replace boot files**
| Replacing the kernel, device tree or FIT image on the boot medium can leave the board unable to start. Keep a known-good SD card or image, copy the old files before overwriting them, and keep a serial console connected so that you can read the boot log.
data.main_content_0_11: Keep every change small, reviewable and in Git. A change that exists only in a working directory is easy to lose and cannot be reproduced.
data.code_content_0_11_0:
$ git status --short --branch
$ git diff --check               # whitespace problems
$ git diff
$ git add <file-you-changed>
$ git commit -m "Describe the kernel change"
$ git format-patch -1 HEAD       # creates a .patch file
data.content_0_11_1: Replace the file name with your own. Keep the patch together with the board name, BSP release, kernel tag and test result.
data.table_caption_0_11_2: Table 8. Standalone build compared with a Yocto-integrated change
data.table_0_11_2_1_1: You need a fast loop to test a kernel or device-tree change directly on the board.
data.table_0_11_2_1_2: Git commits and patches. Artifacts are copied to the board using the documented boot method.
data.table_0_11_2_2_1: The change must be part of a repeatable image build.
data.table_0_11_2_2_2: The patch and configuration fragment are added to a custom layer for the kernel recipe. [1] [5]

data.sub_head_0_12_0: What You Can Change in the Kernel
data.table_0_12_1_1_1: Kernel configuration, driver source and dependencies.
data.table_0_12_1_1_2: A device-tree node, firmware or a userspace tool.
data.table_0_12_1_2_1: An existing or new driver, binding document and device-tree entry.
data.table_0_12_1_2_2: Wiring and electrical design must match.
data.table_0_12_1_3_1: DTS and DTSI files and pinctrl definitions.
data.table_0_12_1_3_2: The matching DTB or FIT image must be packaged and loaded by the boot process.
data.table_0_12_1_4_1: The Kconfig option and the selected configuration.
data.table_0_12_1_5_1: The relevant kernel code and a repeatable test.
data.table_0_12_1_5_2: Regression testing and integration into the BSP build.
data.table_0_12_1_6_2: The module must match the running kernel and be installed in the root filesystem.
data.sub_head_0_12_2: What the Kernel Cannot Fix Alone
data.sub_content_0_12_2: Software cannot replace a missing connection or an unsupported electrical design, and not every system change belongs in the kernel.
data.table_caption_0_12_3: Table 10. Problems and the place to look first
data.table_0_12_3_1_0: A signal is not routed to the connector, or a voltage is missing.
data.table_0_12_3_1_1: Schematic, carrier-board design, power rails and SoM pinout.
data.table_0_12_3_2_0: The board starts from the wrong device or does not load the kernel.
data.table_0_12_3_2_1: Boot configuration, bootloader environment and image layout (BSP-06 to BSP-08).
data.table_0_12_3_3_0: A package or service is missing from the image.
data.table_0_12_3_4_0: The device-tree edit has no effect.
data.table_0_12_3_4_1: The DTB or FIT image that the boot flow actually loads.
data.table_0_12_3_5_0: The application behaves wrongly while the driver works.
data.table_0_12_3_5_1: Application code, libraries and service configuration.
data.table_0_12_3_6_0: A kernel module does not load.
data.table_0_12_3_6_1: Kernel and module versions, dependencies, firmware and dmesg.
data.table_0_13_0_1_0: Repository or tag is not found.
data.table_0_13_0_1_1: Check the spelling, run ``git fetch --all --tags``, and compare with the release notes and recipe.
data.table_0_13_0_2_0: The build uses the host compiler.
data.table_0_13_0_2_1: Source the SDK script in this terminal and check ``echo "$CC"`` and ``echo "$CROSS_COMPILE"``.
data.table_0_13_0_3_0: The defconfig target is not found.
data.table_0_13_0_3_1: Check whether the correct tree and branch are being used. Run ``make help`` and check the board manual.
data.table_0_13_0_4_0: A DTB builds but the hardware does not appear.
data.table_0_13_0_4_1: Check that the correct DTB is built and loaded, then verify pinmux, node status, compatible string, driver and wiring.
data.table_0_13_0_5_0: ``yaml.h`` is missing while building device trees.
data.table_0_13_0_6_0: Kernel boots but a module does not load.
data.table_0_13_0_6_1: Compare the kernel release and module version, check dependencies and firmware, and read ``dmesg``.
data.table_0_13_0_7_0: A manual change disappears in the next image.
data.table_0_13_0_7_1: The change was not added to the Yocto layer or the maintained branch.
data.table_0_13_0_8_0: The board does not boot after an update.
data.table_0_13_0_8_1: Restore the known-good kernel and DTB, then check the serial log.

data.main_content_0_16: This document provides an overview of the PHYTEC Linux kernel source, repository selection, kernel configuration, device-tree customization, and kernel compilation. Following these steps helps developers customize and maintain the Linux kernel for their target PHYTEC platforms.

If the two disagree with the release notes, stop and find out why before you change anything.", "tip_0_8_4": "| **Layouts differ between kernel versions**
| Linux 6.5 moved ARM device trees into vendor folders such as arch/arm/boot/dts/nxp/imx/ and arch/arm/boot/dts/ti/omap/. The AM62x listing still uses the older flat arch/arm/boot/dts/ layout for ARM files, which points to an older kernel base than the others. Always search with find or grep instead of assuming a path, and confirm the version with git describe.", "warning_0_3_1": "| **Repository names change between releases**
| Older PHYTEC documents use other locations, for example stash.phytec.com for i.MX8X PD21.1.0. For i.MX 6UL and AM335x, read the repository and tag from the release notes of your own BSP. The kernel trees of both boards contain PHYTEC defconfigs, which is a useful check after cloning (see the section on PHYTEC files inside the kernel tree).", "warning_0_7_4": "| **Do not copy these commands to another board**
| The repository, tag, SDK path, defconfig and device-tree name are specific to these releases. For another SoC or BSP release, take them from that release notes and manual.", "warning_0_8_6": "| **Start from a clean tree**
| Two of the supplied listings contain files that do not belong to a clean PHYTEC checkout. The i.MX 8M Plus tree has two patch files in its root directory, and the AM335x tree holds ARM device trees in both the old flat path and the new vendor folders. Run git status and git stash list, remove or commit stray files, and rebuild from a known tag before you trust the result."}
